notes: Site: Shopify (nkuku.com, myshopify id 5782274146). robots.txt checked first, no Claude-specific disallow. Access: direct HTTP fetch, no WAF/blocking. Discovery: full mega-menu (desktop + mobile HeaderDrawer markup) parsed from homepage HTML, plus /collections.json (774 handles, 4 pages) scanned for best/popular/trending/favourite keywords. Two genuine Bestsellers-type PLPs found: (1) /collections/bestsellers, nav-linked as 'Bestsellers' with 'Explore Collection' CTA, H1 'Nkuku Bestsellers', on-page copy 'our Nkuku bestsellers showcase the skill and stories of the makers...' -- unambiguous genuine bestseller merchandising page. (2) /collections/bestselling-gifts, nav-linked from the Gifts menu column as 'Bestselling Gifts', H1 matches, distinct product set (gift-scoped bestseller cut) -- kept as its own row per the 'genuinely different listing' rule rather than merged/dropped. Qty for both verified two ways: (a) rendered on-page 'See N items' count badge, (b) exhaustive /collections/<handle>/products.json?limit=250 pagination to empty page, counting unique product IDs -- both methods matched exactly for both listings. The raw /collections.json products_count field was NOT used (confirmed inflated: bestsellers raw=178 matched, but bestselling-gifts raw=100 vs verified/exhausted=90). Checked and EXCLUDED: 'February Favourites' (/collections/february-favourites) -- found only via the /collections.json dump, NOT linked anywhere in current live navigation (0 hits searching homepage nav HTML), raw products_count=97 but exhaustive enumeration returns only 6, H1/copy gave no 'customer favourites/popular' framing beyond the month-dated campaign name -- treated as a stale/orphaned dated marketing collection, not a genuine persistent Bestsellers-type PLP. Also checked footer nav, sitemap-linked collections, and site search (?q=bestseller, q=popular, q=trending) -- no other genuine bestseller-concept PLP found; no sub-structure like 'Furniture Bestsellers' exists on this site (Bestsellers and Bestselling Gifts are flat, unrelated listings, not parent/child).
